context.title: Elisha's Miracles of Life
context.summary: Elisha multiplies a widow's oil, promises a son to a generous Shunammite woman and later raises the boy from death, makes poisoned stew safe, and feeds a hundred men with twenty loaves.
context.background: These stories show God caring for ordinary households in times of famine and debt. Shunem lay in the Jezreel Valley; the Shunammite's family could afford a guest room for the prophet.

customs.note: A creditor could take a debtor's children as servants until the debt was worked off (compare Leviticus 25:39-41).
Probably a bitter, poisonous wild plant that looked like an edible gourd.
The first loaves of the harvest, normally an offering. Here they feed a crowd.

watchFor: The Shunammite's calm 'It shall be well' while her son lies dead (vv. 23, 26).
Elisha stretches himself on the child, as Elijah did (vv. 34–35).

people.name: Elisha
people.summary: God his salvation, the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah, who became the attendant and disciple of Elijah (1 Kings 19:16-19). His name first occurs in the command given to Elijah to anoint him as his successor (1 Kings 19:16).

people.name: Gehazi
people.summary: Valley of vision, Elisha’s trusted servant (2 Kings 4:31; 5:25; 8:4, 5). He appears in connection with the history of the Shunammite (2 Kings 4:14, 31) and of Naaman the Syrian.

places.name: Shunem
places.summary: Two resting-places, a little village in the tribe of Issachar, to the north of Jezreel and south of Mount Gilboa (Josh. 19:18), where the Philistines encamped when they came against Saul (1 Sam. 28:4), and where Elisha was hospitably entertained by a rich woman of the place.

places.name: Baal-shalishah
places.summary: Lord of Shalisha, a place from which a man came with provisions for Elisha, apparently not far from Gilgal (2 Kings 4:42).

events.title: Prophecies of Elisha
events.summary: Passage: 2 Kings 2:15–13:21. People: Elisha. Lasted about 59 years.
